question: Who published the book 'General Morphology of Organism' in 1866 , providing the first definition of ecology as 'the relation of animals to their organic and inorganic environment'?
solution:
The correct answer is '**Ernst Haeckel**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ernst Haeckel **was german zoologist and evolotionist.

 
 
• His book, **General Morphology of Organism** presented several ideas, but the scientific community showed no interest.
 
• Ernst Haeckel saw evolution as a basis of a unified explanation of all nature and denied the beliefs of the church. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alexander Humboldt**, full name - Alexander von Humboldt was a german geographer, naturalist, and explorer. He published several books and was awarded **Copley Medal** for his contributions.

 
 
• He was **one of the most famous men in Europe** during his lifetime.
 
• **Cosmos** was his most famous book, containing all his research work and major explorations.
 
 
 
• **Eugene Odum** was an American biologist known for the introduction of the concept of the '**ecosystem**'.
 
 
• All his work and research lie in the field of Ecology.
 
• The **Ecological Society of America** awards **Eugene P Odum Award** for Excellence in Education of Ecology.
 
 
 
• **Carl Linnaeus **was a Swedish botanist, zoologist, physician, and taxonomist known for '**Binomial Nomenclature Taxonomy**'.
 
 
• **Systema Naturae** was published by Carl Linnaeus in 1735. When its 10th edition was published in 1958, it had **7,700 species of plants and animals.**
